name: Instant-Void
geological_features: Single massive impact crater covering half the surface
description: Instant-Void is a tiny barren body barely qualifying as a planetoid, its irregular shape suggesting it is a rubble pile held together more by luck than gravity. A single impact crater covers nearly half its surface, the blow that created it nearly destroying the body entirely in what must have been an instant of cataclysmic violence.

The negligible gravity means the deep regolith dust behaves more like a fluid than a solid, and surface movement requires tethering to avoid being launched into space by a careless step. The silence and emptiness are absolute, with no atmosphere to carry sound and no features to break the monotony.

The impact that created the great crater scattered debris across the surrounding space, and fragments of Instant-Void have been found in orbit for millions of kilometers around it. The body is slowly dissipating, losing mass to micrometeorite impacts and solar wind erosion, destined to eventually disperse entirely.

The planet has minimal resource value, its iron and carbon deposits too diffuse for efficient extraction. Its primary use is as a navigational marker in an otherwise empty region of space, and as a cautionary example of the fragility of small bodies in the cosmic shooting gallery.
